headline: Tresor condemns Helsing AI military event at Kraftwerk
caption:
Tresor speaks out against a Helsing AI military event at Kraftwerk Berlin.

The Berlin institution issued a statement condemning the event. In its words, such an event "has no place in the spaces our community has built".

headline: Kenny 'Jammin' Jason, Chicago house radio pioneer, dies
caption:
'I miss you already': Farley 'Jackmaster' Funk on his greatest musical mentor, Kenny 'Jammin' Jason.

Jason, a founding member of Chicago's Hot Mix 5 alongside Farley 'Jackmaster' Funk, Mickey 'Mixin' Oliver, Ralphi Rosario and Scott 'Smokin' Silz, has died. From 1981, the Hot Mix 5's WBMX-FM broadcasts introduced wider audiences to house music and the mixing techniques coming out of Chicago's clubs. In 1985 he released the 'Jam Tracks' EP, and he made 'Can U Dance' with Fast Eddie.

article.headline: Kenny 'Jammin' Jason, Chicago house radio pioneer, dies
article.standfirst: Kenny 'Jammin' Jason has died. He was a Chicago DJ, producer and remixer and a founding member of WBMX-FM's Hot Mix 5. Fellow member Farley 'Jackmaster' Funk announced his death on November 19. No cause of death was disclosed.
body: Kenny 'Jammin' Jason has died. He was a Chicago DJ, producer and remixer and a founding member of the Hot Mix 5, the WBMX-FM collective at the centre of the city's early house and radio culture. Fellow member Farley 'Jackmaster' Funk announced his death on November 19, 2026. No cause of death has been disclosed.

Farley paid tribute on Facebook, calling Jason his greatest musical mentor and someone he considered a brother. "I miss you already," he wrote. "RIP. This really hits harder than anyone could know, and I'll tell this story if I'm alive to tell it."

Jason came up through local radio and mobile disco parties, and that groundwork led him to WBMX-FM's Hot Mix 5. The collective was founded in 1981, and its lineup was Jason, Farley 'Jackmaster' Funk, Mickey 'Mixin' Oliver, Ralphi Rosario and Scott 'Smokin' Silz. Their broadcasts introduced wider audiences to house music and to the mixing techniques coming out of Chicago's clubs.

He worked in the studio alongside his radio shows. In 1985 he released 'Jam Tracks', a six-track instrumental EP. His production credits included Liz Torres, and he collaborated with Fast Eddie on 'Can U Dance'. In 1986 he co-founded Hot Mix 5 Records with Oliver and Rosario, which gave Chicago's developing house scene another outlet for its music.

Jason kept DJing in the decades that followed and stayed close to Chicago radio and the local music community. His contribution was recognised with the DJ Kenny Jammin Jason Boulevard naming. In 2016 he reunited with his Hot Mix 5 colleagues to mark the collective's 35th anniversary.
